outcome: effectiveness of pain relief (Visual Analogue Score)
cohort: The study included 50 ASA grade I and II patients, aged 18 to 35 years, who were scheduled for elective caesarean delivery.
finding: The intrathecal bupivacaine-midazolam mixture significantly increased the duration of sensory blockade and analgesia compared to bupivacaine alone, with no significant difference observed in the onset time for sensory blockade, maximum motor blockade, or Visual Analogue Score for pain relief.
